content.text:
Starting with an empty workspace, I'll build tools/minidiff.py using only the standard library—leveraging difflib's SequenceMatcher to find changed line hunks with a line of context, then applying a word-level diff within replaced lines, printing unified-style output and exiting with status 1 if differences exist.

I'm planning the actual output format now: unified headers like `@@ -l,c +l,c @@`, context lines with a leading space, and changed lines marked with `-`/`+`, with word-level substitutions highlighted using `[-old-]` and `{+new+}` brackets so the three substituted words are clearly visible. My plan is to read both files, group line-level opcodes with one line of context via difflib, then for replaced line pairs tokenize into words (splitting on whitespace while preserving it) to mark exactly which words changed, while equal/delete/insert blocks get simpler treatment—plus handling argument errors and missing files with proper exit codes.

I'm drafting two fixture files—a five-line lighthouse passage and a near-identical version with exactly three single-word swaps—to test diffing between them.

I'll place both a.txt and b.txt directly at the workspace root, matching the literal file names requested.

    """Build the @@ -a,b +c,d @@ header for a group of opcodes."""

    a_start, a_end = first[1], last[2]
    b_start, b_end = first[3], last[4]

content.text:
Done. `tools/minidiff.py` is a dependency-free Python 3 CLI (standard library only: `difflib`, `re`, `sys`) that diffs two files at line level, then re-diffs each changed line pair at word level so the specific substituted words are marked: removals as `[-word-]`, additions as `{+word+}`. It prints only changed hunks with 1 line of context and exits 1 on differences, 0 when identical.

**One bug found and fixed.** My first version always wrote the two-number form in hunk headers (`@@ -6,2 +6,1 @@`). Unified diff format omits the length when a range covers exactly one line, so the correct header is `@@ -6,2 +6 @@`. I added a `format_range` helper and re-verified.

**Verification performed:**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Hunk headers vs system `diff -U1`, 5 file pairs | all match, including single-line and empty-file ranges |
| Full output vs `diff -U1` body, word markers stripped | byte-identical |
| All 3 substituted words present | `granite`, `sixty`, `bell` each found |
| Exit code, files differ | 1 |
| Exit code, identical files | 0 |
| Bad argument count / unreadable file | usage or error on stderr, exit 2 |

The three substitutions are `rocky`→`granite` (line 1), `forty`→`sixty` (line 3), and `horn`→`bell` (line 5). Lines 2 and 4 are unchanged and appear only as context. No browser verification applies here, since this is a command-line tool with no web surface.
